extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) dealing with KIPO procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on KIPO examination practice covering handling of conflicting applications, unpatentable inventions (public order/health), and rules/limits for amendments to specifications, claims, and drawings under Article 47 of the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conflicting application with different applicant/inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: A conflicting application whose applicant or inventor is different cannot hold the status of a prior-filed application; an examiner shall conduct examination considering that the conflicting application has never been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conflicting applications rarely occur; often arise when an applicant incorrectly amends claims when filing a divisional. Examiner treats conflicting app as never filed and proceeds accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when conflicting application granted and applicants differ
rubrics_metrics.description: When a conflicting application is granted a patent and the applicants of the present and conflicting applications are not the same, an examiner shall notify the applicant of the conflicting application of such fact through the On-nara System (Government Electronic Document Management System).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notifying a ground for rejection to the applicant of the present application, the applicant shall indicate the fact of conflicting relation in the ground for rejection. Examiner shall check whether a request for examination on the conflicting applications is made when consultation is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for consultation when conflicting application laid open and requested for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflicting application is laid open and requested for examination, the examiner shall make a request for consultation under the name of the Commissioner of KIPO within a designated period, and notify the applicant of a ground for rejection under Article 36(2) or (3) along with the request for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle a request for consultation and a ground for rejection shall be notified in separate notices, but for efficiency the examiner may only make a request for consultation if the contrasting relation can be easily addressed upon consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome after consultation response
rubrics_metrics.description: If after receiving a request for consultation an applicant addresses a ground for rejection under Article 36(2) or (3) by reporting on the result of consultation and taking measures within a designated period, an examiner shall make a decision to grant a patent; where a ground for rejection exists and has been already notified, an examiner shall decide to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely addressing of the notified ground via the consultation process can convert a pending rejection into a grant; failure to remedy leads to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement when conflicting application not laid open/requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflicting application is yet to be laid open or requested for examination, an examiner shall notify the applicant of the present application of the intention that examination is postponed until the conflicting application is requested for examination or withdrawn or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner informs applicant that examination will be deferred pending resolution or request for examination of the conflicting application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when applicants identical and conflicting app granted or finally rejected under Article 36(2)/(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant is identical and a conflicting application is granted with a patent or a final decision to reject is made based on Article 36(2) or (3), the examiner shall issue a notice of rejection to the patent applicant under Article 36(2) or (3) (including other grounds for rejection if present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent is yet to be granted to the conflicting application, examiner shall notify other grounds for rejection to the patent applicant without reviewing Article 36(2) or (3). If other notified grounds remain unremedied after amendment, the examiner will decide to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which ground for rejection to notify (first vs final) depending on amendment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims of the present application are amended later than the date when claims of the conflicting application are finally amended, the final ground for rejection is notified; otherwise, the first ground for rejection is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the consequence (grant/rejection) of the conflicting application is undecided, if it is expected that rejection should be issued under Article 36(2) or (3) upon grant of the conflicting application, the examiner can notify such ground together with other grounds and should request consultation with the patent applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of designated period after consultation request
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for consultation and a ground for rejection are notified at the same time, an applicant intending to extend the designated period may request extension relating to the submission of a written argument as well as the designated period upon a request for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can ask for extension covering both consultation response and written arguments when both notices are simultaneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of a registered patent does not resolve conflicting relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflicting application is registered and no consultation can be made, abandoning the patent or utility model registration does not mean consultation is possible or that the conflicting relation is resolved; abandonment of a registered patent does not have retroactive effect and thus cannot be deemed never filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandoning a patent right by registration is not equivalent to abandoning an application and cannot be used to retroactively remove the conflicting-filed status; doing so would undermine legal security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of invalidation of a registered patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application registered for a patent is determined to be invalidated, it shall be deemed never to have been filed, taking into account Article 36(4) and Article 133(3) of the Patent Act of Korea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation has retroactive effect to treat the registration as never filed; if multiple conflicting registrations exist, invalidation of one does not necessarily invalidate the others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment of patent fees
rubrics_metrics.description: After a patent is granted, where patent fee was not paid in due time for grant or for maintenance or for renewal, the patent is deemed abandoned and thus shall be deemed never to have been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay required fees can render the patent as never filed for conflicting-application purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to rely on other grounds instead of conflicting application
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though there exists a conflicting application, an examiner may make a decision to reject based on other grounds for rejection instead of referring to the conflicting application or notifying a ground for rejection based on the conflicting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Korean Patent Act, an examiner may reject after giving opportunity to submit written argument; the Act does not require citing every possible ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus/species identity rule for conflicting filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A genus invention of a later-filed application is deemed to be identical with a species invention of a prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where filing dates are the same, substantial sameness is assessed by comparing inventions in both role reversals; if not substantially the same in one comparison, they shall not be deemed identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 32 — Public order, morality, and public health bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding Article 29, no invention that violates public order or sound morals or is likely to harm public health is patentable (Article 32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute bar: even if an invention meets patentable subject matter, patentability under Article 29 need not be considered if Article 32 applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'public order' and 'morality'
rubrics_metrics.description: Public order refers to the general interest of society or country and morality means moral sense generally accepted by society or by a particular group; inventions likely to contravene public order or morality are unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent cannot be granted for inventions likely to contravene public order or morality without considering Patent Act objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual aides and private-use exception
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions relating to sexual aides: if the product is quite similar to a specific sexual part of the human body or practicing it is expected to go beyond sexual morals into immoral acts in public, it is deemed against public order/morality; however, if used in private places such that it is impossible to be against public order/morality, the rule will not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess context of use (public vs private) and similarity to sexual body parts when evaluating morality/public order concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions using or harming the human body
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions using the human body which hurt the body consequentially when conducted, inventions that inhumanely block bodily freedom, and inventions damaging human dignity are deemed against public order or morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of natural human wastes (urine, placenta, blood) extracted safely is permitted in general, but food-related uses of such materials for daily ingestion are not accepted for ethical reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper-use exception for public-order assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is not deemed to contravene public order/morality solely due to possible improper use contrary to its original purpose; if the specification clearly discloses an innocuous intended use (e.g., entertainment, not gambling), mere potential improper misuse does not render it unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the intended purpose as disclosed and whether the device is clearly devised for legitimate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of inventions likely to injure public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the manufacturing process itself or the product made by it would injure public health; consider official approvals (e.g., Ministry of Health and Welfare) and whether methods exist to eliminate harmful effects or whether the invention's advantages outweigh risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research showing harm in academic journals alone does not necessarily establish public-health harm if regulatory approval exists; examiner should weigh mitigating measures and net advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend under Article 47 — general timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant may amend the specification or any drawing accompanying the patent application before a certified copy of a decision to grant a patent under Article 66 is served, subject to the specific amendment-period limitations when a notice of ground for rejection has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment opportunities vary depending on whether a non-final rejection, final rejection, or re-examination request is involved; see specific subparagraphs for permitted periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment must remain within original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the specification or drawings shall be made within the scope of the disclosure of the specification or drawings as originally filed; foreign-language applications must also stay within the scope of the final Korean translation as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of new matter beyond original disclosure is prohibited; special rules apply to translations and divisional/converted applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible claim amendments after certain rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the claims made pursuant to Article 47(1)2 and 3 may be made only in cases such as: (1) narrowing claims by restricting/deleting/adding limitations; (2) correcting clerical errors; (3) clarifying ambiguous descriptions; (4) reinstating prior claims under narrow circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims cannot be broadened beyond original disclosure in these amendment periods except as specifically allowed; reinstatement is limited to restoring previously presented claims under defined situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of prior amendments when amending during specified periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application is amended during the period specified in Article 47(1)1 or 2, all amendments made prior to the final amendment shall be deemed voluntarily withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final amendment during those periods supersedes earlier voluntary amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-language application amendment limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding Article 47(1), the specification or drawings of a foreign language patent application may be amended only when a Korean translation has been submitted under Article 42-3(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean translation must be on file before amending spec/drawings of foreign-language filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and retroactivity of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment system addresses incompleteness at filing; where a specification is amended during designated period, the amendment takes retroactive effect to the original filing date. Amendments after start of examination risk invalidating examination results and delaying examination, so amendment periods are strictly limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New matter added via amendment would unfairly take retroactive effect and harm third parties; therefore scope of amendment is strictly limited to prevent undermining first-to-file rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural eligibility to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the patent applicant at the time of amendment may amend the specification or drawings; where multiple applicants exist, not all need undertake amendment proceedings and each may amend individually. The application must be pending before KIPO; if invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, registered for establishment of right, or final rejection is binding, amendment is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency means KIPO can still take necessary administrative actions to grant patent; inactive or final-status applications cannot be amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible amendment varies by amendment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of permissible amendment to specification or drawings differs depending on amendment periods: voluntary amendment period (before start of examination) and period for arguments in reply to non-final rejection allow no addition of new matter; periods for arguments in response to rejection necessitated by amendment and on request for reexamination further restrict permitted amendments to narrowing claims and clarifying errors, etc., and still prohibit new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different remedies and sanctions apply depending on when an illegitimate amendment is made; see handling table (grounds for rejection, decision to refuse entry, invalidation grounds etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of illegitimate amendments depends on timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The method to handle an amendment that does not satisfy substantive requirements differs by amendment period: e.g., during examination an illegitimate amendment may give rise to grounds for rejection; after registration it may be a ground for invalidation; in some periods the examiner may refuse to enter the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the scope-of-amendment table for specific consequences tied to the amendment timing (before delivery of certified copy, within periods for argument submission, on request for reexamination, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and test for 'new matter' (prohibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'New matter' refers to matter which goes beyond the scope of the disclosure of the specification or drawings as originally filed; matters explicitly described or those a person skilled in the art would recognize from the original disclosure are not new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment compares the amended specification/drawings (subject of assessment) with the original specification/drawings (subject of comparison). 'Included in the scope of the disclosure' need not be literal identity; what skilled person would clearly recognize as disclosed counts as included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment rules for new matter — excluded materials
rubrics_metrics.description: First country application or prior-filed application forming the basis of priority shall not be used as the basis of assessment for new matter; abstracts are not part of the original specification for assessing new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the original specification/drawings filed on the application filing date (or divisional/converted equivalents) as the basis for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing an incomplete invention via amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of completing an incomplete invention, the amendment shall be deemed to add new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling in previously missing essential details after filing is treated as introduction of new matter and prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing from genus to species can be new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment narrows a claim from a genus to a species, unless the species is supported by the original specification/drawings or unless a skilled person would readily recognize the species from the genus, the amendment is viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: adding a specific material (e.g., 'ABS') is new matter unless originally disclosed or obvious; substituting 'sensor' with 'proximity sensor' may be supported if a skilled person would intuitively associate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening from species to genus can be new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment broadens a claim from a species to a genus, if the genus includes other species that may have different functions or effects, the amendment shall constitute introduction of new matter. Deleting limitations described as essential is new matter; deleting arbitrary non-essential limitations may be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: broadening geometric detail of a connector leading to changed electrical contact is new matter; deleting an identifying code communication step from traffic-control method may or may not be permitted depending on whether the problems can still be addressed.
